name: 3x22mm Tungsten-Ceramic Flechette TCF-322
description:
The TCF-322 is a magnetically accelerated tungsten-ceramic composite flechette designed for the GFR-3 'Needlerain' repeater platform, optimized for high-volume sustained fire at cyclic rates up to 4,200 RPM. Each flechette is a slender dart with a tungsten core for mass and penetration, jacketed in a ceramic composite that reduces barrel wear and provides consistent electromagnetic interaction with the weapon's gauss acceleration coils.

The flechettes are packaged in sealed 300-round cassettes with electromagnetic advancement — no mechanical feed mechanism, which eliminates the most common failure point in high-cyclic-rate weapons. The cassette is a self-contained unit: flechettes are suspended in a frictionless magnetic cradle and advanced into the acceleration coils by the weapon's own electromagnetic field. This means the feed system has no moving parts and is effectively immune to dirt, moisture, and mechanical jam. The trade-off is that each cassette is a precision-manufactured sealed unit that cannot be field-reloaded — empty cassettes are disposed of, not refilled.

At 1,050 m/s muzzle velocity, each flechette carries sufficient kinetic energy to defeat standard soft body armor at close range, though hard plate remains effective. The weapon's primary lethality comes from volume rather than individual round performance — at full cyclic rate, the GFR-3 delivers 70 flechettes per second, creating a cone of tungsten-ceramic needles that shreds soft targets and degrades hard armor through cumulative impact stress. The ceramic jacket fragments on hard-surface impact, reducing ricochet danger in enclosed spaces but producing a fine ceramic dust that is a documented respiratory hazard in sustained indoor engagements.
specifications:
weight_per_round: 2.1g
muzzle_velocity: 1,050 m/s
penetration_rating: Individual: soft armor only / Cumulative: degrades hard armor over sustained fire
effective_against: Personnel, light vehicles (sustained fire), drones, soft-skinned targets
countermeasures: Hard plate armor (individual rounds), sealed respiratory protection (ceramic dust), magnetic deflection fields
variants: TCF-322 AP (hardened tungsten core, reduced ceramic jacket, increased barrel wear)
TCF-322 Incendiary (phosphor-tipped, ignites on hard-surface fragmentation)
TCF-322 Tracer (every 10th round in cassette, electromagnetic signature visible to compatible optics)
cultural_context: TCF-322 cassettes are a consumable commodity in GLMZ's mercenary economy. The sealed cassette design means they cannot be counterfeited or reloaded — you either have genuine Tessera product or you have nothing. This has made them a de facto currency in some black market circles, where a sealed TCF-322 cassette has a stable and universally recognized value. Operators who carry a GFR-3 typically budget for ammunition as their largest recurring expense, and the weapon's reputation as a 'rich operator's tool' comes as much from the ammunition cost as from the weapon itself. Tessera Corponation has quietly encouraged this dynamic, as it creates a revenue stream that outlasts the initial weapon sale by orders of magnitude.
story_hooks: A Tessera Corponation warehouse containing 40,000 TCF-322 cassettes was hit in a coordinated heist — the cassettes have started appearing on the black market at half price, and Tessera's internal security is offering a bounty that exceeds the street value of the stolen goods.

An independent manufacturer claims to have developed a compatible cassette using reverse-engineered electromagnetic advancement technology — Tessera's legal team has filed injunctions in seven jurisdictions, but the street price of TCF-322 cassettes has already started to drop on rumor alone.
